title: Bank of America CEO addresses a troubling banking problem
detail:
Bank of America CEO addresses a troubling banking problem
Mwangi Enos, Celine Provini
Sat, October 17, 2026 at 2:03 PM MST 5 min read
BAC
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

A few years ago, I remember helping my elderly neighbor set up a new bank account after her branch closed. The process involved more paperwork than buying a car — identity verification, source-of-funds questions, and transaction-monitoring disclosures. 

She found it exhausting. I found it excessive. I remember the banker saying the requirements had gotten stricter "because of what happened with the big banks."

I thought about that incident when the Treasury Department announced more than $1.21 billion in penalties against Bank of America for allegedly doing the opposite.

According to the U.S. Treasury press release, the bank failed to report more than $5 billion in suspicious transactions over several years. Some of that activity was linked to Chinese money laundering networks and operations along the southwest border.

You will most certainly be scrutinized for opening a checking account. The U.S. second-largest bank, meanwhile, was not flagging billions in activity that regulators say included narcotics trafficking proceeds and potential trade-based money laundering.

BAC is down 4.49% year-to-date, according to Yahoo Finance, after falling 2% in after-hours trading on the penalty announcement Oct. 13, the day before CEO Brian Moynihan was scheduled to report Q3 earnings.

Also Read: Bank of America sees another interest-rate surprise

Here is what the Treasury actually found, and why regulators escalated

The $1.2 billion penalty is the third-largest in Treasury history, according to the Treasury announcement. The $750 million civil money penalty from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) is the largest the OCC has ever levied against any bank.

The core finding? Bank of America signed a cease-and-desist order with regulators in 2024 to fix its anti-money-laundering program. Regulators said the problems continued after that order. 

Treasury said the bank "prioritized its revenues" while minimizing compliance resources, and relied so heavily on law enforcement referrals from other institutions that it effectively outsourced part of its own responsibility for detecting suspicious activity.

"Despite its obligation to the American people as a national-chartered, global systemically important bank, the bank's BSA/AML compliance program continues to reflect widespread breakdowns in internal controls, which threatens U.S. national and economic security," Comptroller Jonathan Gould said in the OCC's press release.

title: Bank of America: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
detail:
Bank of America: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
The Motley Fool Team, The Motley Fool
Sat, October 17, 2026 at 11:28 AM MST 3 min read
BAC
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 14, 2026, Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) announced adjusted net income of $8.1 billion. A $1.2 billion regulatory settlement charge reduced reported net income to $6.9 billion. Rising loan yields continue driving core earnings higher. Three things management said stand out.

1. Net Interest Income Growth Will Exceed 8% in 2027

Net interest income, or NII -- the difference between what a bank earns on loans and pays on deposits -- is accelerating as fixed-rate assets reprice into higher yields. Management raised its guidance above original targets.

For 2027, we currently expect full-year growth of NII to be 8% or more, higher than 2026, and again, higher than our original 5%-7% range.
-- Alastair Borthwick, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer

2. Regulatory Settlement Costs Are Already Baked Into Expenses

A $1.2 billion non-tax-deductible regulatory settlement charge for failure to adhere to anti-money laundering compliance lowered reported earnings. Management already built the ongoing technology and staffing costs directly into its standard operating expense base.

Third, we have committed the resources, and the ongoing cost remediation is embedded in our company's expense base.
-- Brian Moynihan, Chair and Chief Executive Officer

3. Low Loan-to-Deposit Ratios Protect Margins From Price Wars

Total deposits reached $2 trillion, funding $1.25 trillion in loans. Because the bank holds substantial excess liquidity, it doesn't need to offer high interest rates to retain customer deposits.

Our focus on operating deposits and our low loan-to-deposit ratio allow us to compete on capabilities rather than price.
-- Alastair Borthwick, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer

Looking Ahead

Commercial borrowing and account growth show no signs of slowing down. Management expects operating leverage -- growing revenue faster than operating expenses -- to resume in the fourth quarter. Fixed-rate loans continue repricing into higher yields, while artificial intelligence tools trim routine technology costs.

What our clients are actually doing is continuing to point to a resilient and growing economy in the U.S.
-- Brian Moynihan, Chair and Chief Executive Officer

Core organic growth in consumer checking accounts and commercial relationships provides a durable moat against market volatility. Broad business diversity insulates total earnings when investment banking and trading activity cool down.

Our balance sheet and capital remain strong, and we continue to invest in technology and develop AI capabilities to support long-term growth. This quarter demonstrates the strength of our franchise and the value of our diversified business model.
-- Brian Moynihan, Chair and Chief Executive Officer

AML Penalty Could Be A Game Changer For Bank of America Stock (BAC)
Sasha Jovanovic
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 1:14 PM MST 4 min read
BAC
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bank of America reported third quarter 2026 results that missed expectations, as a regulatory penalty of more than US$1.21b related to anti money laundering and sanctions compliance weighed on net income of US$6,933m and diluted EPS of US$0.91.

The enforcement orders require Bank of America to overhaul its BSA and sanctions controls, adding ongoing compliance reviews and technology investments that could influence future expense levels and the way the bank runs high risk parts of its business.

We will now look at how this large anti money laundering penalty may reshape Bank of America's broader investment narrative.

Scan how compliance risk is being priced across the sector by reviewing our curated 32 resilient stocks with low risk scores while you assess what this penalty means for Bank of America's long term profile.

Bank of America Investment Narrative Recap

To own Bank of America, you need to believe the large US$2t deposit base, its consumer and wealth franchises, and net interest income focus can keep driving earnings even as capital markets stay softer and expenses remain heavy. The immediate swing factor is execution on expense control while continuing to fund AI and compliance upgrades after the US$1.21b penalty.

The biggest current risk is that regulatory and technology spending pushes the roughly US$18.6b quarterly expense run rate higher just as investment banking and trading fees face pressure. If that happens, the path back to stronger operating leverage and higher returns gets harder, even with solid underlying loan and deposit activity.

The latest batch of results put that tension in sharp focus. Net income of US$6,933m and diluted EPS of US$0.91 reflected the anti money laundering settlement, yet net interest income of US$16,449m showed the basic banking engine at work. For a holder, the key question is how quickly the business can absorb compliance costs without dulling that earnings engine.

Against that backdrop, the new US$90m 6.00% notes due 2032 are worth watching. They underline that Bank of America still has access to fixed income markets to fund its balance sheet and ongoing technology and compliance investments. How efficiently the bank deploys that funding into loans, digital platforms and upgraded controls will shape both future catalysts and how regulators and investors judge execution.

Bank of America's narrative projects US$137.8b revenue and US$38.2b earnings by 2029. This is based on an assumption of 6.6% yearly revenue growth and about a US$6.1b increase in earnings from US$32.1b today.

Interested in Bank of America Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

Bank of America's Q3 revenue grew 3.2% but missed consensus estimates, largely due to an unexpected $1.2 billion money-laundering related legal charge.

A post-earnings sell-off pushed shares below the lowest analyst price target, which analysts view as an overreaction creating a potential buying opportunity.

Reliable dividends, aggressive share buybacks, improving credit trends, and expected NII growth support long-term upside despite near-term interest rate uncertainty.

Bank of America (NYSE: BAC) is a compelling play because of its scale, value, dividend, and sensitivity to interest rates.

While its Q3 results align with the broader financial sector, suggesting a cyclical investment peak in Q2, investors should not get this signal wrong. A peak is a peak, except when the economy is expanding versus contracting.

→ Fundamental and Technicals Signals Align for Costco: Is the Stock Finally Breaking Out?

We're looking at a multi-year, potentially longer economic expansion that has years to play out. Underpinned by AI, data center builds, onshoring supply chains, and favorable government support, the economic backdrop points to sustained growth at Bank of America and additional investment peaks to come.

The only question is timing, i.e., how quickly S&P 500 companies can reload their balance sheets in preparation for the next investment cycle. Between now and then, Bank of America pays a solid capital return, and its shares have returned to trend.

→ Palantir's Potential Next Catalyst After Retail Profit-Taking

Technically, BAC's market reverted to trend following its Q3 earnings release, indicating potential for a trend-following entry in mid-October. Support is marked by the converging long-term 150-week exponential moving average and 2022 highs. The EMA is noteworthy because it represents long-term buy-and-hold investors, such as the institutional group, which owns more than 70% of the stock and whose activity coincides with 2026's stock price bottom.

Side-by-side long-term and short-term stock price charts for Bank of America showing a plunge, trend line, and rebound.

→ Bank of America Stock Sell-Off Looks Like a Buying Opportunity

Q3 Earnings Reveal Strength Beneath the Headline Miss

Bank of America didn't have a bad quarter, just a weaker one than expected, compounded by an unexpected legal charge. Authorities tagged BAC with a $1.2 billion charge tied to money-laundering controls and reporting, which impacted net earnings in the quarter. Revenue grew 3.2% to nearly $30 billion, missing consensus by more than $600 million, or 200 basis points. Strengths came from the Consumer and Global Wealth Management segments, which grew 4% and 13%, respectively, while weakness in Global Banking and Global Markets offset gains.

(Updates with Bank of America's response in the last paragraph.)

Bank of America (BAC) has launched a sale of investment-grade bonds, Bloomberg reported Friday, citing a person familiar with the matter.

The bank is marketing the bonds in as many as four tranches with maturities ranging from three to 11 years, the report said, adding that the longest-dated tranche is initially being offered at a yield premium of about 1.2 percentage points to Treasuries.

Bloomberg reported that Bank of America was the only one of the six major Wall Street banks that did not tap the high-grade bond market in the third quarter. The bank has raised $17 billion so far in 2026, the least among the group, according to the report.

A Bank of America spokesperson declined to comment to MT Newswires.
